stats.fact: Kontext CLI has 210 GitHub stars and 7 forks as of August 2026
Kontext CLI has shipped 20 releases from v0.5.0 to v0.16.0 between May and July 2026
Kontext CLI received 70 upvotes and 17 comments on Hacker News Show HN (April 2026)
Kontext CLI is built with Go 1.25 and released under MIT license
Kontext supports Claude Code, Claude Cowork, and Codex with pre-tool-use blocking
Kontext Guard uses SVM classifier with 0.987 precision and Qwen3-0.6B guardrail LLM with 0.585 precision for risk classification
Kontext Guard risk classifier processes decisions in ~22ms without LLM, ~200ms with LLM
Kontext was originally at kontext-dev/kontext-cli, moved to kontext-security/kontext-cli

angles: Kontext is the only credential broker that combines runtime security (pre-action enforcement) with credential brokering in a single CLI tool
Unlike competitors that only broker credentials, Kontext also provides policy enforcement, audit trails, and risk classification
Kontext's local-first architecture means decisions stay on the developer's machine — no cloud dependency for every tool call
The IETF CB4A draft is formalizing the credential broker pattern — Kontext is an early implementation of this emerging standard
Kontext supports both standalone (local-only) and managed (cloud dashboard) modes, giving teams a graduated adoption path
The credential broker space is rapidly heating up in 2026 with multiple OSS tools emerging (Postern, Sesame, BlindVault, AgentWrit)
